i.norm: Verifies that flatten() collapses a sparse argument array (mostly nulls) containing one unrecognised multi-character short option ("-Z&=") into a single-element result. The 6-element array has null at every position except index 4. With stopAtNonOption=false and an empty Options set, the parser does not know "-Z", so burstToken() falls into the "unknown option, keep going" branch and emits the whole token unchanged. Null entries are skipped. The net result is one token.

Build a 6-element argument array; only slot 4 carries a value. The token "-Z&=" is longer than two characters and starts with "-", so PosixParser will attempt to burst it. Because "Z" is not a registered option and stopAtNonOption is false, the whole token is emitted as-is.
Only the one non-null token should appear in the output.
